result:
Never-Sold looks at you and waits.
Topics:
  1. Is there more to do?

Never-Sold: "There is. A fire went through Blackrose Prison, which the families born there call the Rose. The heirs of those families brought three held there out of the smoke. They keep them at their stone house on the east shore of Blackrose. The three are Says-It-Plain, Hides-In-Reeds and Keeps-The-Old-Count, who is Rows-For-Another's mother. The keeper, Third-Born Tsaxi, might count one of them lost to the smoke for good words or for coin, I think. Here are a hundred gold for him. They are yours to keep if words do the work. From here go south-east through Blackrose to the shore. The stone house stands at the water's edge. Tsaxi stands outside its west wall, on the town side. I will not say which one should go. Hear all three first, in the house's one room."

Keeps-The-Old-Count: "I came to the Rose with nowhere else to go, the season my daughter was taken onto the estate. The heirs gave me a place by their fire. I ate what they gave me and was glad of it. They have counted that shelter ever since. The count is larger with each season. When I die, the heirs will look to my daughter for what I ate. That is a debt she never sat down to. I will not tell you mine is the better case. The two beside me were held for what they did or said, and I am old, with fewer years to give. I have not seen my daughter since the season she was taken, and I would see her again."

I would say it again."
